newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela chemical sector contracts 6.6 pct in 96.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela chemical sector contracts 6.6 pct in 96.

text.p: Venezuela's chemical and petrochemical industry contracted by 6.63 percent in 1996, but industry officials said Monday they expect a recovery this year.
Gross sales fell $200 million to $2.9 billion in 1996, according to the Venezuelan Association of Chemical and Petrochemical Industries (Asoquim).

Falling world prices, recession overseas and Venezuela's domestic economic crisis all contributed to the decline, which was greater than for manufacturing sector as a whole. Manufacturing contracted by 5.82 percent last year.
Asoquim said Venezuela's domestic recession was reflected in a 14 percent fall in chemical and petrochemical imports.
The figures were announced by Asoquim president Hernan Morales, who expected a sharp recovery in 1997.
"The sector could grow by about five percent, which would reverse the fall in 1996," he told journalists.

Venezuela's domestic market was expected to pick up on an increase in purchasing power following recent social security agreements signed between government and unions. And heavier investment would accelerate the change.

"Expectations are high for investments associated with the liberalisation of the oil sector and the planned investment of the industry itself," he said, adding that the country's macroeconomic indicators were looking more stable.
However, "we have still not conquered inflation nor have we brought more security to the legal and fiscal environment."
State-owned Pequiven and its associated companies account for 41 percent of sector sales, Morales said. The sector as a whole accounts for 24.5 percent of Venezuela's non-oil exports.
The sector showed a trade deficit of $165 million in 1996, against $530 million in 1995, and Morales expected to show a surplus within five years.
